raw.details:
Description

  • The Quantum Magnetometry Challenge is an online individual analytical competition based on simulated quantum-magnetometer data. Participants will analyze extremely weak magnetic-field variations, identify meaningful patterns in the measurements, and determine the likely source or signature associated with the observed variation.
  • Participants must process the provided data, apply suitable analytical techniques, and submit the required results along with supporting analysis, code, plots or parameter estimates as specified by the organizers.
  • Submissions will be evaluated using the published criteria. Qualifying participants may be shortlisted for the offline phase based on the announced selection threshold and verification process.

Duration

Total Duration: 90–120 minutes

Rules & Guidelines

1. Eligibility

  • Participation is individual.
  • Participants must satisfy the eligibility requirements specified in the official event announcement.
  • Participants must provide accurate registration information.
  • Participants must meet any additional requirements specified for consideration for the offline phase.

2. Competition Format

  • Participants will receive a simulated quantum-magnetometer dataset and an associated problem statement.
  • The objective is to detect weak magnetic-field variations and determine the likely source or signature of the observed variation.
  • Participants must submit their analysis and required outputs through the designated platform.
  • The competition is conducted online.

3. Dataset Usage

  • Participants must use the dataset and data sources provided or explicitly permitted by the organizers.
  • Hidden test data or evaluation information must not be accessed.
  • Participants must not manipulate the evaluation dataset.
  • External datasets may only be used when explicitly permitted by the competition rules.

4. Analysis Requirements

Participants may perform appropriate analytical operations such as:

  • Data preprocessing
  • Signal analysis
  • Noise reduction
  • Feature extraction
  • Statistical analysis
  • Pattern detection
  • Magnetic-field variation detection
  • Source/signature identification
  • Model-based analysis

The exact permitted methods and resources will be specified by the organizers.

5. Submission Requirements

Participants may be required to submit:

  • Final result/source identification
  • Numerical measurements or parameter estimates
  • Analysis code
  • Relevant plots/visualizations
  • Methodology or technical explanation
  • Any additional files specified by the organizers

All submissions must follow the required format.

6. Evaluation & Scoring

Submissions may be evaluated based on:

  • Accuracy of weak-signal detection
  • Accuracy of source/signature identification
  • Quality of analytical methodology
  • Robustness of the solution
  • Reproducibility
  • Required numerical/performance metrics

The exact evaluation metric and scoring weights must be published before submissions begin.

7. External Resources & AI Tools

The use of external datasets, software, online resources and AI-assisted tools will follow the official competition policy.

Participants must comply with any restrictions or disclosure requirements.

8. Originality

  • Participants must independently develop their analysis unless collaboration is explicitly permitted.
  • Copying another participant's code, analysis or results is prohibited.
  • Similarity or integrity checks may be performed.
  • Violations may result in disqualification.

9. Technical Verification

Qualifying or unusual submissions may be reviewed to verify:

  • Correctness of results
  • Reproducibility
  • Dataset compliance
  • Analytical methodology
  • Use of permitted resources
  • Absence of hidden-data leakage

Participants may be asked to provide supporting evidence where required.

10. Offline-Phase Selection

  • Participants will be considered for the offline phase according to the published qualification threshold, advancement criteria and available slots.
  • Eligibility and technical verification will be completed before the shortlist is confirmed.
  • Tie-break rules will be applied according to the published competition rules.

11. Disqualification

A participant may be disqualified for:

  • Ineligible participation
  • Unauthorized access to hidden data
  • Data leakage
  • Manipulation of evaluation data
  • Use of prohibited resources
  • Copying another participant's work
  • Unauthorized collaboration
  • False or misleading results
  • Submission after the deadline
  • Violation of the published competition rules

12. Final Results

The online results and offline-phase shortlist will be confirmed after the required evaluation and verification process.
